STEP 1 - Vessel type: flat square plate (white, rim band visible, flat centre, no inner wall).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This plate looks like a standard dinner-size square plate, so about 25 cm.
b) Reference: the pizza slices are roughly 11-12 cm along their crust edge, and the plate spans roughly two slice-lengths plus margin across its width, which suggests about 24-27 cm.
Reconciled width: 25 cm (area 625 cm²).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Pizza slices: 2 visible slices (one with tomato and meat, one cheese). Each slice is a countable standard piece at about 30 g... but these are larger wedges, so I estimate each at roughly 100 g of pizza (crust, cheese, sauce, topping), giving about 200 g total.
- Spinach/leafy salad: covers roughly 40% of the plate, about 250 cm². Loose leaves 3-6 cm deep, but mostly a thin spread with some mound; take average 2 cm. Volume 250 × 2 = 500 ml × 0.15 (raw) = 75 g.
- Mushrooms (about 4 small cooked pieces): about 4 × 15 g = 60 g.
- Red onion slivers and tomato wedge (tomato is on pizza, counted there): onion ~5 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: pizza slices sit on the salad area; the base is mainly the plate. No substantial hidden layer beyond the greens already counted. Total around 340 g.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g:
- Pizza (cheese, meat, crust): about 270 kcal/100 g.
- Raw spinach/mixed greens with light dressing: about 25 kcal/100 g.
- Cooked mushrooms (sautéed): about 60 kcal/100 g.
- Red onion: about 40 kcal/100 g.

Item energy:
- Pizza: 200 g × 2.7 = 540 kcal
- Greens: 75 g × 0.25 = 19 kcal
- Mushrooms: 60 g × 0.6 = 36 kcal
- Onion: 5 g × 0.4 = 2 kcal
